newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No Australian car report this week - govt official.
newsitem.headline: No Australian car report this week - govt official.

text.p: A crucial report on Australian government automotive policy will not be published this week, a government official said on Monday.
"Nothing is going to appear in the immediate future," said the official, who asked not to be named.
In a draft version of the report issued in December the Industry Commission urged the government to slash vehicle tariffs to five percent by 2004 from the current 25 percent.
The official said the final report would go to Treasurer Peter Costello, the minister responsible for the commission, on Monday.
Earlier, the Adelaide Advertiser newspaper said the report would not appear until the government had formulated a policy in response.
The newspaper also said the commission would miss the target of delivering the report on Monday.
Meanwhile, the Australian Democrats, a minor party, called on the government to publish the report as soon as it had been delivered and not to wait until it had developed the policy.
The Australian automotive industry supplies much of the domestic market, partly with vehicles designed elsewhere and partly with models of entirely local origin.
Four car makers have Australian manufacturing operations -- Ford Motor Co, General Motors Corp, Toyota Motor Corp and Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
